title: Drain the water off a pan of dumplings into the sink, keeping every dumpling in the pan
instruction: Drain the water from the pan into the sink but keep all the dumplings in the pan, then set the pan back on the stove.
context: Draining pasta, potatoes or dumplings by holding the lid ajar is an everyday kitchen move: one hand tips the pan, the other holds the lid just open enough to let the water out and keep the food in. A lid that is not held slides off as the pan tips, and the food goes into the sink with the water.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. In a real trial a thin waterproof bench liner covers the table under the stove and the sink. (1) A fixed stove block standing in for a cold burner: a dark grey round block (wood or any rigid material), 10 cm across and 13 cm tall, centred 27 cm forward and 1 cm right of the centre line. (2) On it, centred, a loose 12 cm stainless-steel milk pan: inside 11 cm across and 7.5 cm deep (0.7 L); a 0.8 mm wall (11.16 cm across outside); a 5 mm floor (the 0.8 mm steel floor, an aluminium disc 9.5 cm across and 3.7 mm thick, and a 0.5 mm steel cap 9.8 cm across); and a solid black phenolic handle bar 7 cm long, 2.5 cm wide and 2.2 cm tall, riveted on just under the rim and pointing straight back toward the arms. 0.385 kg in all: steel 258 g, aluminium 71 g, handle 54 g, rivets 3 g. (3) Its lid, loose and centred on the rim: a flat 0.6 mm stainless-steel disc 13.6 cm across with no rim or skirt (it overhangs the rim by 1.2 cm all round), and on top a solid black phenolic knob 2.2 cm front to back, 3 cm side to side and 5.2 cm tall, held by one M5 screw. 0.119 kg: disc 69 g, knob 48 g, screw 2 g. The README works out every mass from density x volume (steel 7.93, aluminium 2.70, phenolic 1.40 g/cm3). (4) In the pan, six dumplings and their water. In a real trial: six Mrs. T's Mini Classic Cheddar Pierogies (frozen potato-and-cheddar dumplings; 13 g each, from the label's 11 pieces = 143 g), boiled from frozen as the package says (into 4 quarts of boiling water, back to the boil, 3 minutes), rinsed 30 s under cold tap water and set in 300 ml of tap water at 35 to 45 degrees C (about 4 cm deep with them in); a fresh portion every trial. In simulation: six pale yellow balls 24 mm across, 13 g each, in a ring on the floor, and 20 blue beads 5 mm across, 0.5 g each, each standing for 15 ml of the water (20 x 15 ml = 300 ml). (5) The sink: a fixed white polypropylene collecting basin with no drain, inside 16 cm square and 6.6 cm deep (1.7 L; its rim 7 cm above the table; 4 mm walls and floor), centred 41 cm forward and 1 cm right of the centre line, in front of the stove; everything around it is open table. It is a small plugged basin, smaller than a kitchen sink, and a real trial uses a basin of that size (for example a square plastic tub). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 unless the pan ends standing on the stove (tilted less than 10 degrees, its centre within 4 cm of the stove's). Otherwise 1.0 with at least 240 ml of the 300 ml collected in the sink and all 6 dumplings in the pan; 0.5 with at least 150 ml collected in the sink and at least 5 dumplings in the pan; 0.25 with at least 75 ml collected in the sink and all 6 dumplings in the pan; else 0.0. Only water that ends inside the sink basin counts: water on the table, the stove, the floor, the outside of the basin or anywhere else is spilled and never counts as drained, and water left in the pan does not count. A dumpling that is not in the pan at the end, or that left the pan at any time during the trial (even if it was put back; judged from the trial video), is lost, wherever it ends; dumplings that end in the sink are counted separately and never count as water; a dumpling that splits counts where its larger part ends. In a real trial the basin is plugged, empty and dry at the start. After the trial any dumplings in it are lifted out with a slotted spoon, shaken over it and counted; then the water collected in it is poured into a measuring jug (10 ml marks) or weighed in the basin on a kitchen scale (1 g resolution, the dry basin's weight taken off; 1 g = 1 ml). The dumplings in the pan are counted, and the trial video is checked for any that left the pan and were put back. In simulation each water bead stands for 15 ml and counts as collected only if its centre ends inside the basin (inside its walls, above its floor and below its rim): 1.0 needs at least 16 of the 20 water beads (240 ml) there, 0.5 at least 10 (150 ml), 0.25 at least 5 (75 ml); dumplings in the sink are counted separately as lost dumplings, and a dumpling whose centre is outside the pan's inside at any control step is lost. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the pan and every bead still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Throw away the used pierogies (those in the pan and any in the basin); never reuse or reboil them. Empty, rinse and dry the sink basin and stand it back plugged and dry; rinse and dry the pan and the lid; dry the table, the bench liner and the stove. Boil a fresh portion as the package says: 7 pierogies straight from the freezer (6 and a spare) into 4 quarts of boiling water, back to the boil, 3 minutes; rinse them 30 s under cold tap water. Pour 300 ml of tap water at 35 to 45 degrees C (checked with a kitchen thermometer) into the pan, lower six unbroken pierogies into it with a slotted spoon, spread over the floor, stand the pan on the stove with its handle pointing back and centre the lid on it; start within 10 minutes of the boil. In simulation: put the 20 water beads and the 6 balls back.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). The water is 20 rigid 5 mm beads, 15 ml each, that pour but do not flow or cling and weigh 10 g, not 300 g: the pan hand lifts 0.47 kg here, 0.76 kg in a real trial. The pierogies are rigid 24 mm balls of their real 13 g. The pan wall and lid disc are 3 and 4 mm thick here, not 0.8 and 0.6 mm, for stable contacts, with the real masses (0.385, 0.119 kg). Temperature is not simulated.
